stance_summary: October ASX 30-day AONIA still prices a near-full 25bp RBA hike after a September hold, while dated housing-channel evidence and a cooling labor/activity mix argue the next decision/averaging window is the mechanism that forces that hike out. Global post-FOMC/BoJ tightening can keep the contract rich until that local event. Hold the existing receive; do not duplicate AONIA_2026-10.

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Receive AONIA_2026-10 (long duration): packet implied 4.565 versus overnight AONIA 4.35, i.e. +21.5bp, the liquid contract that owns the next RBA decision and October averaging window.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short AUDUSD: packet spot 0.712022367194781 as of 2026-09-18, 1y percentile 76.4 and 5y percentile 84.3, as the FX expression of an RBA skip into housing stress.
expression_comparison.rationale: The mispricing is a dated policy-path probability in one IB contract, not an FX level. AONIA_2026-10 is the instrument that settles to October realized AONIA, so the next RBA decision/averaging window reprices it directly. AUDUSD is only a 76th-percentile 1y residual with Fed, energy and USD noise; AUDNZD is a 5y extreme but NZ rates are unavailable so the cross cannot be risk-matched. Rates is cleaner and executable from the frozen AONIA strip.

context_build.causal_mechanism: FACT: overnight AONIA is 4.35 as of 17-Sep-2026; September IB is 4.355 (+0.5bp) so a September hike was not delivered; October IB is 4.565 (+21.5bp) with open interest 21752 and volume 4450. INFERENCE: the RBA cash-rate reaction function is being asked to hike in the October window despite an already-open housing-credit channel (NSW stamp-duty receipts -24% y/y in August, transaction volumes -18%, Sydney and Melbourne values more than 7% below peak). A hold/skip in that window lowers realized October AONIA toward the current overnight fixing and forces the 2026-10 contract to reprice lower. UNKNOWN: the packet does not print the exact next RBA calendar date.
context_build.path_to_current_price: FACT: AU 2Y 4.999 and 10Y 5.348 as of 2026-09-16 sit at the 99th percentile of both 1y and 5y samples, with 2Y +39.1bp over 1m and -5.5bp on the last day; the AONIA strip then rises from 4.355 (Sep) to 4.565 (Oct), 4.685 (Nov), 4.725 (Dec) and about 4.94 by mid-2027. Fed funds were raised 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on the 16 Sep decision after >90% hike odds, and the BoJ raised 25bp to 1.25%. INFERENCE: AU front-end richness is a mix of sticky local inflation levels plus global hike spillover after those decisions, not a fresh local activity boom. The 1d AU yield dip did not cheapen October IB, which remains +21.5bp versus overnight.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: KNOWN: inflation is still hot in level terms (AU inflation gauge 82; July trimmed mean 3.6% y/y unchanged; headline 3.5% after 3.8%). NEW relative to a September hold: 16 Sep Reuters housing evidence that the tightening channel is already cutting transactions and state tax take; July employment -15.8k and unemployment 4.5% after 4.4%; August RBA business conditions/confidence softer; September Westpac-MI sentiment -5.2% to 84.4. ALSO NEW as spillover: the Fed hike and BoJ hike, which the desk thesis says keep term-rate pressure elevated even where domestic growth is softer. INFERENCE: October IB has not decayed because markets are looking through housing via global tightening and the inflation level, which is exactly the priced assumption the October event can break.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: FACT: October IB at 4.565 versus overnight 4.35 is +21.5bp, about 86% of a 25bp hike inside the October averaging window; November at 4.685 is +33.5bp. INFERENCE: the market requires the RBA to deliver a 25bp October hike with high probability and to keep a residual additional tightening into November, treating housing and labor softening as non-binding for the next meeting.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: The assumption that the RBA can still look through an already-open housing channel and validate nearly a full October hike. The disagreement is not that inflation is low — it is not — but that the dated next decision cannot ignore stamp-duty/volume/price destruction, weaker jobs, and a September sentiment collapse once September itself was a hold.
context_build.price_decomposition: FACT: the 2026-10 contract is a 30-day AONIA average, not a 2Y bond; overnight 4.35 is the starting point; September IB 4.355 shows no in-month hike; the entire +21.5bp of October is therefore the marginal hike-odds component. Further strip steepening (Nov +33.5bp, Dec +37.5bp, 2027-06 +59bp) is extra-cycle, not required for this expression. AU 2Y 4.999 is a blended policy-plus-term-premium level at a statistical extreme and is not a substitute for the IB path. Spot AUDUSD 0.712 is mid-high versus 1y history and is a residual, not the hike-odds object.

historical_reference.distribution: FACT: AU 2Y/5Y/10Y are all at the 99th percentile of 1y and 5y samples; AU 2s10s is 34.9bp (24th percentile 1y). The AONIA 2026-10 contract is 21.5bp above the official overnight benchmark with the strip's highest listed volume (4450) and open interest 21752. INFERENCE: the sovereign curve is already pricing a restrictive regime; the live discrepancy is concentrated in near-dated hike odds, not in a cheap 10Y.
analogs: The frozen packet does not contain a compiled event-study of prior RBA holds versus fully priced 30-day IB contracts, so no quantitative analog with forward outcomes is available. The qualitative comparison is a hiking/holding central bank that has already opened the housing-credit channel while inflation remains above comfort, with the structural twist that this October contract already embeds almost a full hike so a skip — not a hike — is the surprise.
historical_reference.regime_differences: Inflation gauge 82 and trimmed mean 3.6% mean the RBA can still justify a hike in a way a clear disinflation analog would not. Global policy is tightening (Fed 3.75-4.00%, BoJ 1.25%, BoE 6-3 hold with three hike votes), so spillover can keep AU front-end rich even if local housing is the binding constraint. Energy-shock narratives remain two-way. NZ rates are missing, so AU-NZ policy RV cannot be used as a confirming analog.

trade.thesis: FACT: the book already receives AONIA_2026-10 at 4.565, equal to the frozen packet mid, with September IB at overnight. Housing-channel evidence from 16 Sep shows stamp-duty and prices already contracting; labor and September sentiment have softened while inflation remains a high level. INFERENCE: the dated path to repricing is the next RBA decision and the October AONIA average — a skip/hold collapses the +21.5bp hike-odds component toward 4.35, while a hike delivered as priced is largely in the contract (asymmetric). Global Fed/BoJ tightening is the reason that component can stay rich until that event. UNKNOWN: exact meeting date, whether October CPI prints first, and RBA weight on inflation 82 versus housing. Do not open a second AONIA_2026-10; hold pos-deddf5aa0c83.
trade.mispricing: October IB prices +21.5bp versus overnight AONIA 4.35 (~86% of 25bp) after a September hold and after documented housing-channel damage. That is too much October hike for a cash-rate decision that must confront an already-open tightening channel.
why_now: September IB is already at the overnight fixing, so the live fight is the October averaging window and the next RBA decision — a dated mechanism, not a valuation slogan.
The 16 Sep housing print arrived after that hold and has not cheapened October IB, which still marks 4.565, identical to the existing entry.
Fed and BoJ hikes since then are a plausible spillover keeping AU hike odds rich; that spillover is unwound when the RBA has to vote on local housing, jobs and sentiment.
Funded-seat SOFR vig accrues whether flat or invested; the existing receive is the only packet-supported path that can beat that vig if the skip hits.
